Smt. Barkha Rani vs Nitin Chandaliya (2024:Rj-Jd:50257) on 9
December, 2024
Author: Rekha Borana

Bench: Rekha Borana [2024:RJ-JD:50257]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Civil Transfer Appl. No. 158/2024 Smt. Barkha Rani W/o Nitin Chandaliya, Aged About 30 Years,
D/o Shri Tejmal Ji Ranka, R/o Kapasan Ps Kapasan, Dist.
Chittorgarh, At Present R/o Bada Baag, Asind, Police Station Asind, Dist. Bhilwara (Raj.)
 ----Petitioner  Versus Nitin Chandaliya S/o Rajendra Chandaliya, R/o Kapasan, Police Station Kapasan, Dist. Chittorgarh (Raj.)

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Manas Khatri for  Mr. N.K. Gurjar
For Respondent(s) : None present  HON'BLE MS.
JUSTICE
REKHA BORANA Order 09/12/2024 1.

The present transfer application has been preferred by the petitioner-Wife seeking transfer of the Divorce Petition bearing No.33/2024 titled as Nitin Chandaliya vs. Barkha Rani filed under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as, 'the Act of 1955') by the respondent-Husband before Family Court, Chittorgarh to Family Court, Bhilwara.
2. As averred in the petition, the marriage between the petitioner and the respondent was solemnised on 15.08.2012 as per Hindu rituals and customs.
However, after some time there were instances of harassment and continuous demand of dowry by the respondent-Husband and his family.
Aggrieved by the actions of the respondent-Husband, the petitioner-Wife lodged an FIR under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Subsequently, the respondent-Husband filed the aforesaid application under Section 13 of the Act of 1955 before Family Court, Chittorgarh.

1 3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner-Wife submits that she is currently residing in her parental home at Bhilwara and is financially dependent on her parents.
The petitioner is pursuing LL.B. and has examinations ongoing due to which it is difficult for her to repeatedly attend court proceedings at Chittorgarh.
Further, she is required to travel every now and then the long distance between Chittorgarh and Bhilwara, without any support.

4. Additionally, an application bearing No.302/2023 (Annexure- 1) under Section 125 Cr.P.C. has already been filed by the petitioner-Wife at Bhilwara and the respondent-Husband is duly attending the proceedings.
Therefore, the application under Section 13 of the Act of 1955 as filed by the respondent-Husband at Chittorgarh be also transferred to Bhilwara.

5. Although service on the sole respondent is complete, none has put in appearance.
6.
Heard counsel for the petitioner and perused the material available on record.

7. In view of the submissions made, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner having no source of income of her own, definitely would be facing financial hardship and inconvenience in travelling from Bhilwara to Chittorgarh time and again to attend the proceedings at Chittorgarh.

8. A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Ekta Dhadhich vs. Rajendra Prasad Sharma; S.B.
Civil Transfer Application No. 72/2021 (decided on 30.09.2021) while relying upon the judgment of Asma Praveen vs Javed Bhati; 2018 (4) RLW 3511 (Raj) observed that the comparative hardship is more to the wife and when proceedings related to same parties are [2024:RJ-JD:50257] (3 of 3)
[CTA-158/2024] pending, the Court should primarily consider the convenience of the female litigant.

entities.text: Ekta Dhadhich vs. Rajendra Prasad Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Asma Praveen vs Javed Bhati; 2018 (4) RLW 3511 (Raj)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Co-ordinate Bench observed as under:
"16.

It is well settled legal position that while going into the merits of a transfer application, Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants, and transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
In such type of matters, the convenience of the wife is to be preferred over the convenience of the husband."
9. In view of the above position of law, the present application is allowed.
The Petition No.33/2024 pending before Family Court,
Chittorgarh is directed to be transferred to Family Court, Bhilwara.

10. The Family Court, Chittorgarh is directed to send the complete file/record of Petition No.33/2024 (Nitin Chandaliya vs. Barkha Rani) to the Family Court, Bhilwara within a period of two weeks from the receipt of the certified copy of the present order.
